issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court may dissolve a marriage under its constitutional power when the marriage is emotionally and practically dead, even though the asserted statutory ground of cruelty was not proved, and may make dissolution conditional on property being transferred to the other spouse.
material_facts: The spouses had lived apart for about twenty-five years, and their marriage was described as dead emotionally and practically, with no realistic prospect of its revival.
The lower courts found that serious allegations made by the wife about the husband's character were unsupported by evidence and could not establish cruelty.
The husband had failed to meet his responsibilities toward his wife and son, but the son was grown and in service.
The husband expressed remorse and offered to transfer his only house to his wife as compensation for his past conduct.
issues.conclusion: The Court exercised its power under Article 142 to dissolve the marriage, subject to the husband transferring the house to his wife and handing over possession; the dissolution would take effect upon both acts.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(1)(i-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 provides for divorce on cruelty, and V. Bhagat v. D. Bhagat (Mrs) explained the concept of mental and physical cruelty. Chanderkala Trivedi (Smt) v. Dr. S.P. Trivedi recognized that where a marriage is dead and cannot be retrieved, it is better to bring it to an end. In this case, despite the failure to prove cruelty, the Court used Article 142 of the Constitution to end the dead marriage on the stated condition.

rule.if: matrimonial_dissolution_appeal and prolonged_separation and marriage_emotionally_and_practically_dead and no_realistic_prospect_of_retrieval and continued_marital_tie_prolongs_agony and statutory_cruelty_ground_not_proved and applicant_expresses_remorse and applicant_offers_property_transfer

predicates.matrimonial_dissolution_appeal: A party appealed in a proceeding seeking dissolution of a marriage.
predicates.prolonged_separation: The spouses had lived apart for a prolonged period.
predicates.marriage_emotionally_and_practically_dea: The marriage had ceased to function emotionally and practically as a marital relationship.
predicates.no_realistic_prospect_of_retrieval: There was no realistic prospect that the marriage could be restored.
predicates.continued_marital_tie_prolongs_agony: Continuing the marital relationship would prolong the spouses' agony and affliction.
predicates.statutory_cruelty_ground_not_proved: The evidence did not establish the asserted statutory ground of cruelty.
predicates.applicant_expresses_remorse: The spouse seeking dissolution expressed remorse for past conduct.
predicates.applicant_offers_property_transfer: The spouse seeking dissolution offered to transfer property to the other spouse.
predicates.marriage_dissolved_on_property_transfer_: The marriage is dissolved once the offered property has been transferred and possession delivered to the other spouse.

issues.definition: When a dissolution appeal concerns a prolonged, irretrievable, emotionally and practically dead marriage, the asserted cruelty ground is unproved, and the applicant expresses remorse and offers a property transfer, the rule provides for dissolution upon that transfer and delivery of possession.
